accessibility-information-preserved-part: Preservation is not guaranteed for all accessibility information, e.g. alternative text for embedded images can be lost or become non-descriptive during a copy-and-paste process, and table semantics from the source document are not reliably retained. Authors are advised to review pasted output, but no in-tool warnings flag dropped accessibility information.
accessible-components-available-partiall: Core built-in components were independently audited (March 2026; see our Accessibility Conformance Report), but third-party plugins are not evaluated, and the plugin gallery does not indicate accessible options; plugin accessibility varies and relies on plugin developers to comply.
accessible-content-production-possible-p: Structured metadata fields and rich text formatting with headings/lists make accessible content production possible, but accessibility-relevant options (like image alt text) are not prominently surfaced or prompted; authors can produce accessible content without being guided to it.
alt-available-partially-description:
Most essential controls and images expose text alternatives, but several gaps remain. Small action icons (edit, delete, view) often lack descriptive labels, forcing reliance on visual cues alone; statistics graphs and charts lack text alternatives, making data points inaccessible to screen reader users; and some logos, and institution (ROR) icons are missing alt text. 
The dashboard presents many identical "View" links that screen reader users cannot distinguish. Each issue is tracked publicly in our Accessibility Conformance Report with linked GitHub issues; fixes are part of the ongoing remediation cycle.
alternatives-manageable-partially-descri: Alt text and caption fields are available for image uploads and rendered in published output, but there is no mechanism for the dashboard's statistics charts, and providing alternatives is not enforced; tracked in our public Accessibility Conformance Report.
auto-content-accessible-partially-descri:
OJS generates published article pages, journal homepages, and email communications from the Default Theme. The front end was audited (March 2026) and performs well overall but does not yet fully conform to WCAG 2.2 AA. 
Accessibility of submitted manuscript files (e.g., author-produced PDFs) remains the responsibility of each author/journal, as documented in PKP's accessibility statement scope.
comments: Submission by the Public Knowledge Project (PKP/SFU), developers of Open Journal Systems, Open Monograph Press and Open Preprint Systems. Conformance evidence: independent accessibility audit by Access Changes Everything (March 2026) covering reader and editorial interfaces of all three platforms, tested by paid auditors with disabilities using JAWS, NVDA, Narrator, VoiceOver and braille displays; published VPAT at https://docs.pkp.sfu.ca/acr-vpat/en/ with per-criterion ratings and linked GitHub issues. Remediation of identified barriers began Q3 2026.
documentation-promotes-accessibility-par: PKP Docs and the accessibility documentation aim to be accessible; PKP's website statement notes its own web properties are still working toward verified WCAG 2.1 AA conformance end-to-end.
enough-time-partially-description: No time-based limits are enforced on user sessions in the editorial interface. An auto-save timer announces itself in a way testers found distracting; this is tracked for improvement in the Q2 2027 remediation cycle
features-promote-accessibility-partially: Semantic structure, responsive layout, and labelled metadata fields are on by default in the standard theme, but accessibility features are not surfaced or explained in the editing workflow; users must consult documentation to discover them.
navigate-by-structure-partially-descript: Focus order and navigation order generally follow a logical sequence, and multiple ways to reach pages exist (menu, breadcrumbs, dashboard links). But heading hierarchy has known problems: missing or invisible page H1s, duplicate headings, and over-use of H2 on landing pages, and page titles in the editorial dashboard do not change per view. Tracked in the Github issues Accessibility Roadmap to be included in constant release for the LTS version.
presentation-programmatically-determined: Status and save notifications are announced programmatically, but some custom widgets and dynamic components expose state incorrectly to assistive technologies; tracked in our public Accessibility Conformance Report.
prevent-mistakes-partially-description:
Rich text editors include standard undo/redo for content edits, and destructive workflow actions (declining or deleting a submission) require explicit confirmation before taking effect. However, there is no general undo for workflow actions themselves. 
Changes like sending a submission to a new review stage, modifying settings, or bulk edits to submissions generally cannot be reversed by the user. 
Some form flows also lose edits when errors occur. These limitations are noted in our audit and will inform upcoming remediation work.
previews-accessible-partially-descriptio: Published galleys (HTML, PDF) are previewed/read in the browser. The accessibility of generated galleys depends partly on files uploaded by authors. We will assess and update this answer.
tool-description:
Open Journal Systems (OJS) is an open-source journal management and publishing platform developed by Public Knowledge Project (PKP). It manages the full editorial workflow: author submissions, peer review, editing, scheduling, and publication. It also publishes journals online.
OJS is used both as an authoring environment ( authors can submit their manuscripts and editors create announcements and editorial communications) and as a publishing platform for readers.
web-based-accessible-partially-descripti: OJS is fully web-based. Most core editing, submission, and editorial-workflow screens are keyboard operable, honour browser text scaling and text spacing, and were tested by independent auditors with disabilities using JAWS, NVDA, Narrator, VoiceOver, and braille displays (audit completed March 2026). The tool does not yet fully conform to WCAG 2.2 AA: known gaps include drag-and-drop reordering without a keyboard alternative, rich text editors that are hard for screen readers to use, reflow problems at 200–400% zoom in editorial views, and incomplete form error messages. Each gap is documented per WCAG success criterion (with linked GitHub issues) in our public Accessibility Conformance Report. Remediation is underway; fixes are tracked on our public roadmap, and the report is updated as releases ship.
works-with-keyboard-partially-descriptio: All core functions are operable by keyboard, and no keyboard traps were identified. However, some complex interactions are not yet fully keyboard-accessible: reordering by drag-and-drop lacks a keyboard alternative, and rich text editors can trap focus or require undocumented key combinations to exit.
